subject: Clarification: default storage & automated purge examples for prompts/outputs
messages:
From: Elena Morris <elena.morris@fintera.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Jul 2028 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Info request: what Redwood keeps by default (prompts/outputs)

Hi Ava / Marcus,

We're completing a short security questionnaire ahead of pilot kickoff and need concrete examples for what Redwood stores by default for hosted API customers. Specifically: 
- Do you persist prompt text and model-generated outputs by default? If so, for how long?
- What metadata is always retained (IP, model version, token counts, timestamps)?
- Are any parts of requests treated as ephemeral and never written to disk (KV cache, transient-only telemetry)?
- Do you have automatic purge windows or only manual delete APIs?

I've attached our RFI to show the exact fields they're asking for. A quick table or example rows would be ideal. Can you send examples (e.g., customer request X keeps: request metadata for 90d, prompt/text 30d) so I can paste into the doc?

Thanks,
Elena

Fintera Bank

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Jul 2028 11:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Info request: what Redwood keeps by default (prompts/outputs)

Hi Elena — thanks for the RFI, good questions. Below are concise, example-backed clarifications you can drop into the questionnaire. I'll also attach a small CSV with example rows that map RFI fields to our default behavior.

Summary (hosted API default):
- Request metadata (timestamp, model id, token counts, route, region): retained 90 days for diagnostics and billing.
- Prompts (user-provided input) and model outputs (generated text): retained by default 30 days and then permanently deleted from our hot stores unless the account enables "persist_conversations" for debugging or fine-grained quality analysis.
- Embeddings/derived vectors: not stored unless explicitly enabled by the customer (opt-in).
- KV cache / runtime-only state: never persisted to durable storage for hosted API (evicted after model session ends).
- Telemetry traces (error rates, token counts): aggregated metrics kept for 365 days; raw traces containing full prompt/output content are subject to the 30-day rule above.

Automatic purge behavior:
- We run a background purge job that marks objects for deletion at the retention window, with physical deletion completed within 24–72 hours depending on workload.
- Customers can trigger immediate bulk deletes via the control-plane API (DELETE /v1/accounts/{account_id}/stored-objects?type=prompts). Deletes perform a soft-delete followed by background physical purge.

Private & Dedicated differences (important for Fintera):
- Private (VPC/on-prem): by default, data residency and retention are controlled by the customer's deployment config. If you request a stricter retention window in the contract, we will configure the instance to honor that window and can enable customer-managed keys for audit archives.
- Dedicated (redwood-managed GPUs for a single customer): defaults are identical to hosted but can be narrowed via committed config in the SOW.

Attached: retention_examples.csv — three example rows mapping RFI fields to our defaults.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call if you want to walk through examples with your legal/security folks.

Best,
Ava Chen
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Ava — couple of follow-ups for our InfoSec checklist: 
1) Residency guarantee for EU customers: if we set region=eu, does any replication or backups cross regions?
2) We need to confirm deletion propagation: when we call the delete API, how do you ensure backups and any async replicas are also removed? Is there a certified timeline?
3) Is there an API trace / audit log we can ingest to show deletion occurred (for our auditors)?
4) Are DB snapshots or longer-term archives ever written to cold storage (>90 days) by default?

Quick answers here are fine — we can formalize in the contract, but the above will help us sign off on pilot.

Hi — following up with the technical details to address the Sec team questions. Sorry for the longer note, wanted to be explicit so you have language for auditors.

1) Residency / replication:
- For EU-region accounts (region=eu) hosted in eu-west-1, primary and async replicas are kept within the same region by default. We do not cross-replicate to other regions unless cross-region failover is explicitly enabled in the account settings (we would document that and require customer consent).

2) Delete API & propagation:
- API: DELETE /v1/accounts/{account_id}/stored-objects?type=prompts
- Behavior: the object(s) are soft-deleted immediately (status: deleted). The deletion event triggers an internal fan-out that marks related indices, caches, and replication pointers for removal. Physical purge of content occurs via background jobs; worst-case propagation to all replicas/backups completes within 48 hours for normal workloads. We provide a deletion-event id you can reference.

3) Audit evidence & logs:
- We provide an audit feed you can subscribe to (push or pull) that includes deletion events, including deletion_event_id, timestamp, initiating API key, and affected object ids. For EU Private deployments we can deliver the audit feed to your SIEM via syslog or a customer-configured S3 bucket.

4) Snapshots / cold archives:
- By default we do not write customer prompts/outputs to long-term cold archives beyond the configured retention window. Short-term snapshots (for quick restore) are maintained for up to 7 days and are subject to the same region and key policies.
- If you request extended archival for reasons like regulatory retention, that is a contract-level opt-in and will be stored in encrypted archives (SSE-KMS or customer-managed key) and retained per agreed schedule.

5) Practical example (to paste into your RFI):
- "Default hosted behavior: prompt text & outputs — stored 30 days; background purge completes within 24–48h after retention expiry; immediate soft-delete on API call with deletion_event_id; short-term snapshots kept up to 7 days; no cross-region replication for EU unless explicitly enabled."

Attachments: deletion_api_spec.json (stub) — includes example request/response and the deletion_event_id payload we return.

If you'd like, we can provide a signed data handling addendum with the exact deletion SLA language for contract insertion. Happy to coordinate with your legal.

Regards,
Marcus Lin

Redwood Inference
